messages.subject: Error in spatialShrunkenCentroids
messages.body_plain:
I have noticed that since upgrading to Cardinal 2.4.0, I have been getting this error when running spatialShrunkenCentroids.

Error in if (all(class == pred$class)) break :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Although I'm not completely sure, it seems that this error may be related to the k parameter? I loaded an MSProcessedImagingExperiment from Cardinal 2.2.6 that previously segmented with no issue but was also unable to perform segmentation so I assume there was a change in how SSC processes data since then. messages.subject: Re: Error in spatialShrunkenCentroids
messages.body_plain:
Upon further inspection, I have found the error. In like Line 223 of stats2-spatialShrunkenCentroids.R, it seems that when a pixel of class <NA> is present depending on the dataset and/or parameters SSC uses. The all() function therefore produces NA when they are present, which throws an error in the if statement on Line 223. Do you have any suggestions on how to deal with these "bad pixels"?

As a temporary fix, I have made some changes to the source code in the following functions in the stats2-spatialShrunkenCentroids.R file to attempt to handle NA values in SSC (highlighted in red):

.spatialShrunkenCentroids2_cluster <- function(x, r, k, s, mean, class, weights,
                                                dist, iter.max, BPPARAM)
{
    iter <- 1
    init <- TRUE
    # suppress progress in inner parallel loop
    progress <- getOption("Cardinal.progress")
    options(Cardinal.progress=FALSE)
    on.exit(options(Cardinal.progress=progress))
    # suppress messages
    verbose <- getOption("Cardinal.verbose")
    # cluster the data
    while ( iter <= iter.max ) {
        options(Cardinal.verbose=FALSE) # suppress messages
        class <- factor(as.integer(droplevels(class)))
        if ( nlevels(class) == 1L )
            .stop("singular cluster configuration, try a different seed")
        fit <- .spatialShrunkenCentroids2_fit(x,
            s=s, mean=mean, class=class, BPPARAM=BPPARAM)
        pred <- .spatialShrunkenCentroids2_predict(x,
            r=r, class=class, weights=weights, centers=fit$centers,
            sd=fit$sd, priors=NULL, dist=dist, init=init, BPPARAM=BPPARAM)
        compareClasses <- function(c1, c2) {
            same <- (c1==c2) | (is.na <http://is.na>(c1) & is.na <http://is.na>(c2))
            ifelse(length(same[is.na <http://is.na>(same)]) > 0, FALSE, TRUE)
        }
        if ( compareClasses(c1=class, c2=pred$class) )
            break
        class <- pred$class
        init <- pred$init
        iter <- iter + 1
        options(Cardinal.verbose=verbose) # print progress now
        .message(".", appendLF=FALSE)
    }
    options(Cardinal.verbose=verbose) # restore
    .message(" ")
    list(class=pred$class, probability=pred$probability, scores=pred$scores,
        centers=fit$centers, statistic=fit$statistic, sd=fit$sd)
}

.spatialShrunkenCentroids2_predict <- function(x, r, class, weights,
                            centers, sd, priors, dist, init, BPPARAM)
{
    # suppress progress in inner parallel loop
    progress <- getOption("Cardinal.progress")
    options(Cardinal.progress=FALSE)
    on.exit(options(Cardinal.progress=progress))
    # calculate spatial discriminant scores
    fun <- function(xbl) {
        .spatialScores(xbl, centers=centers, weights=attr(xbl, "params"),
            neighbors=attr(xbl, "neighbors"), sd=sd + s0)
    }
    s0 <- median(sd)
    scores <- spatialApply(x, .r=r, .fun=fun, .blocks=TRUE,
        .simplify=.rbind_and_reorder, .init=init, .dist=dist,
        .params=weights, BPPARAM=BPPARAM)
    if ( isTRUE(init) ) {
        init <- attr(scores, "init")
        attr(scores, "init") <- NULL
    }
    if ( is.null(priors) && !is.null(class) )
        priors <- table(class) / sum(table(class))
    scores <- scores - 2 * log(rep(priors, each=ncol(x)))
    colnames(scores) <- colnames(centers)
    # calculate posterior class probabilities
    pfun <- function(scores) {
        s <- exp(-0.5 * scores)
        pmax(s / rowSums(s), 0)
    }
    probability <- pfun(scores)
    colnames(probability) <- colnames(centers)
    # calculate and return new class assignments
    class <- factor(apply(probability, 1, function(x) ifelse(length(x), which.max(x), NA)),
        levels=seq_len(ncol(centers)), labels=colnames(centers))
    list(scores=scores, probability=probability, class=class, init=init)
}

I realize that Cardinal is still actively being worked on so this may have already been addressed, but if not I'm wondering if a fix or suggestion on how to handle the data could be made? I have also tried Cardinal 2.5.1 but gotten the same error so far. Thanks again!

messages.body_plain:

I have a file with a few empty spectra. All pre-processing methods work fine, except for baseline reduction with the locmin method:

mse_pre <- reduceBaseline(msidata, method="locmin")
mse_pre <- process(mse_pre, BPPARAM=MulticoreParam())

processing [reduceBaseline] ...
Error: BiocParallel errors
  element index: 348, 349, 350, 351, 352, 353, ...
  first error: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

--> first element index corresponds to first empty spectrum

It would be great if the function could be fixed to be consistent with the other pre-processing functions...

Thanks,
Melanie
